correctness.rationale: Original three-stage 3D Douglas–Rachford with commuting directional Laplacian lifts eliminates to R=I+3PxPyPz−PxPy−PxPz−PyPz. Entries according to 0,1,2,3 different coordinates have signs determined by 1+3abc−ab−ac−bc, p(3bc−b−c), pq(3c−1), and 3pqr respectively. Positive inverse offdiagonals and minimal endpoint diagonals d_n=D_{n−1}/D_n make each of the three 3d_i d_j≥d_i+d_j necessary and sufficient for n_i≥2 and Δt>0. Continuant D_n recurrence plus monotone resolvent gives cubic d_n≥2/3, unique τ_n↑(3−√6)/2 and τ_2=(√7−1)/6. An independently constructed exact 8×8 rational Kronecker step at s=7/25 yielded min entry −3241875/3189506048 and 24 negative entries. Infinite all-grid result rests on analytic entry classification, not this finite example.

originality.rationale: The original 1956 three-dimensional Douglas–Rachford scheme and unconditional stability are established prior facts, but stability does not ensure positivity of every matrix entry. The exact pairwise resolvent-diagonal inequalities and finite-grid sharp thresholds appear absent from inspected modern positive-ADI records. The 1956 paper and 1962 follow-up were blocked in fresh authorized full-text retrieval (Oxford VPN disconnected), so originality is a qualified best-of-knowledge PASS with material historical risk, not a claim of complete original paper noncoverage.

value.rationale: Monotonicity/positivity is a separate numerical-analysis property from the original Douglas–Rachford unconditional stability. Sharp all-rectangular-grid pairwise conditions, the finite-n cubic threshold curve, and an exact sign counterexample quantify when the original 1956 three-dimensional scheme violates discrete maximum principles. The claim is specific to the identified scheme and avoids claiming later ADI methods.
